reference: Braun AW 10 as revised by Dietrich Lubs in 2018, the AW 10 EVO (39 mm), followed in the colourway it shares with the 1989 original: a black bezel ring on a matt stainless-steel case, with a black dial. The EVO is the only AW 10 found with a date; the 1989 original (33 mm, catalogued as 'chrome and black') and its 2017 re-edition have none, and Braun's AW 20 of 1990, which has a date, has no black ring and is a separate model. The dark ring in the drawing is the AW 10's black bezel ring; the drawing shows nothing of the case behind it. An all-black EVO also exists (ring, case block and crown all black, bolder numerals) and would be equally consistent with the drawing; the classic colourway is preferred here only because it is the one the 1989 AW 10 had. One drawn detail matches no AW 10: on the real watch the date takes the place of the numeral 3 and shows pale figures on a dark disc with a small red caret beside it, whereas the drawing keeps the 3 and sets a white window inboard of it.

surfaces.material: black bezel ring: plastic on the 1989 AW 10 ('reinforced plastic' in Wallpaper; a Braun design catalogue speaks of its 'black plastic ring'); the EVO ring material is not confirmed (one retailer reportedly lists plastic)
surfaces.detail: Black ring with a flat top and softly rounded edges and a fine, slightly pebbled matt surface, no chamfer and no polish; it overhangs the case block behind it. Lubs says of the EVO that the black ring around the dial 'masks out the light'; the surface is read from Gear Patrol's photographs.

surfaces.part: other (thin ring between the bezel and the dial)
surfaces.material: not stated; probably the rim of the metal case around the crystal
surfaces.detail: A thin ring shows just inside the bezel at the edge of the crystal: pale silver with an even soft sheen on the steel-and-black watch, dark grey on the all-black one. It shows no mirror reflections in the photographs. Whether it is the case rim, a crystal seat or a dial flange is not stated anywhere.

surfaces.material: stainless steel, matt; black on the all-black colourway (coating type not stated)
surfaces.detail: The flat rectangular block that shows above and below the ring is evenly matt silver-grey with crisp, unpolished edges. Sources say only 'matt stainless steel'; the photographs show no brush lines, so 'blasted' is an inference.
The same matt finish on the straight sides, almost entirely hidden behind the ring from the front.
Tiny ribbed crown at 3 set so low that it only just peeks out from under the bezel ring; no guards. Its ribs can catch a small glint.
Flat, even matt black with no texture, rings or sheen ('a simple matte dial').

Numerals in a plain grotesque (no 3 on the EVO, where the date sits), minute strokes with longer strokes at the hours, the Braun logo and 'Made in Germany', all flat matt white print ('painted hour markers'); the all-black EVO uses a bolder weight.
Two flat white baton hands with square ends; no lume, no bevel and no bare metal showing.
Hair-thin custard-yellow hand with a short tail and a large round yellow hub that caps the centre over the white hands.
A plain rectangular cut-out at 3 in place of the numeral, with no frame or bevel; a small bright red caret is printed at its left edge, pointing at the date.
A dark disc with pale numerals sitting just below the dial surface (read from Gear Patrol's photographs).
Flat mineral crystal lying within the bezel ring ('a flat mineral crystal'); no dome and no magnifier.

surfaces.part: bracelet or strap at the lugs
surfaces.detail: Smooth matt black leather as wide as the case block where it meets it, butting square against it with no visible lugs or gap, then tapering slightly.

lightBehaviour: Almost nothing on this watch sparkles. Dial and bezel ring stay near-uniform dark from any angle, told apart only by slightly different blacks and a soft sheen along the edges of the ring.
The one crisp reflection is the flat mineral crystal: a single flat patch of glare that crosses the dial when the lamp is near the line of sight.
White hands and numerals are paint, so they stay flat white under any lamp, and the yellow seconds hand stays flat yellow.
The matt steel block shows a broad soft gradient, never a sharp highlight; there are no polished edges anywhere. On the all-black colourway the block is as dark as the ring.
The thin ring inside the bezel and the tiny crown are the only parts that can show a faint line of light.
geometry: A round bezel ring sitting on a narrower, flat, straight-sided case block: from the front, a circle with a rectangular tab above and below that is as wide as the strap. The EVO is 39 mm across. The black ring is about a fifteenth of the diameter wide on each side, flat-topped with rounded edges; inside it a thin ring (about a third as wide) and a flat crystal. The crown at 3 is tiny and tucked under the ring. The lug tabs are square and straight and, on the EVO, end in a 45-degree slope toward the wrist. The date opening sits at 3 in place of the numeral. No crown guards, no pushers.
avoid: Do not add shine: no polished chamfer on the ring, no brushed steel with polished bevels, no gloss or ceramic look on the black ring.
No lume, no applied markers and no raised print; everything on the dial is flat matt paint.
The seconds hand is yellow with a large yellow hub. Red belongs only to the tiny date caret.

A white date disc with black figures set inboard of a retained 3, as in the baseline drawing, is not found on the AW 10, the AW 20 or the AW 10 EVO. The real EVO date replaces the 3 and is pale on dark; the 1989 AW 10 has no date at all.
Do not draw conventional curved lugs; the strap meets a flat rectangular block of its own width.
Do not dome the crystal or make it sapphire-bright; it is flat mineral glass.

Only the ring is black on the classic colourway: the block behind it is matt silver steel. Do not blacken the block unless the all-black EVO is deliberately being followed, and do not make the ring metallic on either.
